title: Speed Limits
whatItIs: The speed limit is the most you may drive on that road, not a target. The national limits depend on the type of road and your vehicle.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT drive faster than the speed limit for the road and for your vehicle.

keyFacts: Roads with street lights are usually 30 mph, unless signs show a different limit.
A white circle with a black diagonal stripe means the national speed limit applies.
Drive slower when conditions call for it: rain, fog, ice, darkness or lots of pedestrians.

visual.caption: National speed limits in mph (signs can set a lower limit)

b.label: A number in a red ring

onTheTest.question: You see the national speed limit sign on a single carriageway. What is the limit for a car?
onTheTest.why: On a single carriageway the national limit for cars is 60 mph. It is 70 mph on dual carriageways and motorways.

traps: The national speed limit sign doesn't mean 70 mph everywhere: it depends on the road and the vehicle.
A limit is a maximum. In bad weather the safe speed can be much lower.
